Game teardown · 16:07 · 56 markers reviewed

BREAKAWAY — Incremental Cycling

watch · 10

A side-scrolling idle cycling prototype that maps power, incline, distance, rivals, training cycles, and achievements onto an always-moving ride.

Visible cycling journey × training resets × passive FP × later race specialization
Developermbjerre

Released4 Sep 2026
AI statusCreator explicitly described it as non-AI

Why Radar kept it

3,000creator-reported browser plays in the first week
~429/daylower-bound average inside that reported launch window
specific feedbackpower, hills, speed, copy length, and ride feel discussed independently

The number is self-reported and plays are not unique users, but the feedback is product-specific rather than congratulatory. Players discussed whether Power felt impactful, whether hills scaled convincingly, and why movement could feel slow. That makes BREAKAWAY more valuable than a higher-view prototype with no mechanical response.

Play / developer page3,000-play reportitch feedback 1itch feedback 2

Observed system

Initial action: Space or clicking the cyclist produces pedalling. Automatic Pedaling costs 15 FP and quickly removes repeated input. Cadence Drills then trade FP for percentage Power, raising speed and future generation.

Visible simulation: speed, gradient, elevation, distance, total climb, and ride time sit over the moving landscape. Power is capped against a current maximum; inclines reduce speed while roadside cyclists make relative pace visible.

Training prestige: the first cycle needs 200 run FP and resets current FP plus training upgrades for 2× pedalling gain. Later fitness levels multiply FP by 4× and 8× while cycle targets expand to 2,800, 12,940, then 62,372.

Achievements: fitness and distance milestones add passive FP/s. The broader source describes races, money, equipment, adaptation, skills, and track specialization; the recording does not reach those systems, so they remain product claims rather than observed loop depth.

Persistence surfaced

  • Three rider career slots
  • Rider head and team-kit customization
  • Automatic progress checkpoints during play
  • Manual Save Game
  • Profile export and import
  • Reload persistence was not independently retested

Session arc

Automatic pedalling arrives within the first minute. The first 200-FP reset lands around 03:36, Fitness Level 1 follows immediately, and achievement passive income begins to compound. By 09:43 the player has Level 2 and 41.95 FP/s; by 13:38 Level 3 produces 81.77 FP/s with 17,736 lifetime fitness. The numbers accelerate dramatically, but the visible activity remains riding, buying training rows, completing cycles, and inspecting achievements.

Strong · numbers have a body

Power changes cadence, incline changes speed, distance moves the scenery, and other cyclists provide relative motion. The idle economy is grounded in an understandable physical object.

Strong · early prestige teaches compounding

The first reset arrives quickly, states exactly what will disappear, and offers a simple permanent reward. It makes the incremental grammar explicit.

Friction · unlock inflation

Targets jump from hundreds to tens of thousands before a new verb appears. Faster FP does not fully offset the feeling that the player is waiting for the same panel to change.

Friction · Power lacks a decisive demonstration

The HUD exposes watts and terrain, but one purchase rarely produces an unmistakable overtake, hill win, or timing improvement. This matches the independent feedback Radar captured.

Recommendations

Stage a first mini-race

After the first cycle, introduce a 20-second rider challenge where a Power upgrade visibly changes the result. Pay a small permanent reward.

Compress system reveal

Open one Adaptation choice at Level 1 and one equipment slot at Level 2, even if full racing remains later. New verbs should accompany multiplier jumps.

Quantify each purchase in the world

Show predicted speed on the current incline, time to the next landmark, and which nearby rider becomes beatable after buying the upgrade.

Screen-by-screen product anatomy

Interface specification

A reconstruction-oriented inventory of the visible hierarchy, controls, states, interruptions, and feedback in BREAKAWAY — Incremental Cycling. It describes observed recording evidence first; recommendations are explicitly labelled.

Evidence convention. Observed means the state is visible in the reviewed session or captured UI. Implementation guidance marks a production requirement inferred from the interaction model, not a claim about unseen code.

Viewport map

Top telemetry band

Persistent ride variables—speed, incline, elevation, distance, climb, ride time, power, and Fitness Points—form a compact instrument panel. Values must remain legible over motion.

Road and rider stage

The side-view road occupies the visual center. The rider sits low in frame while terrain, rivals, and roadside details move past, making otherwise abstract incremental progress physical.

Action and progression edge

The manual pedal prompt is immediately reachable; training, achievements, and later cycle controls open as adjacent panels rather than replacing the ride for long.

Controls, components, and states

The prompt should depress or pulse and the FP/power readout should update in the same frame.

Provide motion, volume, contrast, and number-format controls without making players lose the current ride.

Overlays & interruptions

  • Save-slot and rider-customization screen before the active road.
  • Training and achievement panels layered over or beside the continuing ride.
  • Roadside speech bubbles that interrupt visually but not mechanically.
  • Training Cycle confirmation with current multiplier, next multiplier, reset list, persistent list, cancel, and confirm.

Motion, VFX & feedback

  • Road parallax, wheel/pedal animation, and rider bob translate clicking into travel.
  • FP, FP/s, cadence, power, and speed changes receive short value flashes or floating deltas.
  • Purchases snap into the owned state; achievement and cycle completions deserve distinct celebratory bursts.
  • Incline changes alter posture/pace and terrain movement so the physics-flavored numbers feel causal.
  • Reduced-motion mode should keep numeric and color feedback while limiting parallax and camera shake.

Responsive, accessibility & edge cases

  • Keep the manual target at least 44×44 px and preserve keyboard activation; do not make rapid clicking the only accessible input.
  • Collapse telemetry into two readable rows on narrow screens instead of shrinking every label.
  • Format large values consistently and explain abbreviations; preserve exact values in tooltips where rounding is used.
  • Autosave around purchases and cycle resets, then show a brief saved/error state without stealing focus.
Reconstruction test. A new player should identify the pedal input in three seconds, unlock passive motion without opening documentation, explain every displayed ride value, and predict exactly what a Training Cycle removes and preserves before confirming it.

Creator context · verified public sources

Developer dossier

Who made BREAKAWAY — Incremental Cycling, the public context around the work, and the nearest verified projects. Private identity, location, employment, and credits are left unknown unless the creator or an official project page states them.

Public identity and credit

The project is published by mbjerre, the public creator handle used on itch.io and in the launch discussion. The itch profile describes the active work as “Project Breakaway.” No separate studio credit is asserted by the reviewed official pages.

Location and working context

A real name, city, country, employer, and team size were not publicly verified. The safest description is an independent creator working under the mbjerre handle; the cycling theme and English-language posts do not establish geography.

Timeline

The prototype appeared publicly in early September 2026; the game page lists 4 September, and the creator reported roughly 3,000 browser plays during its first week. Public replies show the developer collecting feedback on power, hills, perceived pace, UI, and progression soon after launch.

Other verified work

The official itch profile showed only BREAKAWAY / Project Breakaway at the research date. No other shipped game could be verified, so this dossier does not convert experiments, likes, or followed creators into a portfolio.

Visible development pattern

The visible pattern is rapid public prototyping followed by specific feedback triage. The creator has discussed reworking presentation and progression and explicitly described the project as non-AI-made in the linked launch conversation.

What this means for the teardown

Treat the recorded version as an early, moving target. The core cycling/reset model is reconstructable, but UI hierarchy and balancing are likely to change; retain dates on screenshots and do not attribute later revisions to the captured build.

Identity boundary. mbjerre is a public account name, not a verified legal identity. No location or prior catalog is inferred where the official profile is silent.

04
Reconstruction blueprint

What must exist to rebuild the observed game

This is a product and systems specification derived from the public build and the recorded first session. It describes observable behaviour, not the original source-code architecture.

Reconstruction confidence. High for the 16-minute training loop, cadence, FP economy, cycle resets, achievements, NPC riders, and save/export UI. Medium for races, equipment, specialisation, and late progression described outside the reached session.

State machineSession flow

  • Profile / rider setup → choose a save slot, import/export option, and rider appearance.
  • Manual start → press Space or click the rider to pedal and earn initial Fitness Points.
  • Automation unlock → spend 15 FP on auto-pedalling and let FP/s sustain forward movement.
  • Training loop → buy cadence/power upgrades while speed, incline, watts, distance, and climb evolve.
  • Cycle reset → meet the current FP target, reset current FP/training, and multiply future gain.
  • Milestones → achievements add passive FP/s; riders/dialogue punctuate the road; later systems promise race and equipment progression.

Input contractControls

  • Space or clicking the rider performs the initial/manual pedal action.
  • Mouse purchases training, completes cycle resets, inspects achievements, handles save/export, and customises the rider.
  • After automation, observation and upgrade timing replace continuous input.

Rules engineSimulation and resolution

  • Fitness Points are the main training currency and are generated manually, then per second.
  • Auto-pedalling unlocks at 15 FP in the observed onboarding.
  • The HUD maps abstract output to speed, incline, elevation, distance, climb, ride time, watts, FP, and FP/s.
  • Cadence drills and training purchases raise production; terrain changes the physical presentation of progress.
  • Cycle targets observed include 200, 2,800, 12,940, and 62,372 FP, with multipliers progressing through ×2, ×4, and ×8.
  • A cycle reset removes current FP and training upgrades but permanently accelerates the next climb.

Meta layerEconomy and progression

  • Achievements unlock at milestones and contribute passive FP/s, adding a second compounding layer.
  • By the end of the session the rider reached Fitness Level 3, 81.77 FP/s, and 17,736 lifetime fitness.
  • Passing cyclists and short dialogue make output visible in the world even before competitive races unlock.
  • The broader product loop advertises races, winnings, equipment, and rider specialisation, but those were not reached.
  • Autosave, manual save, profile export, and import are visible; actual reload recovery was not tested.

Required screen and interface inventory

Save-slot selection, import/export, and new profile
Rider customisation
Road scene and comprehensive cycling HUD
Manual pedal prompt and auto-pedalling unlock
Training/cadence purchase panel
Cycle completion and multiplier reset
Achievement tiles and passive gain
Passing riders and dialogue
Save/profile controls
Later race, equipment, and specialisation surfaces inferred from product copy but not recorded

Minimum useful data model

  • RiderStats: current/lifetime FP, FP/s, watts, cadence, fitness level, permanent multiplier, training levels.
  • RideState: elapsed time, distance, route position, incline, elevation, climb, speed, nearby rider events.
  • TrainingDefinition: cost curve, additive/multiplicative output effect, reset persistence policy, unlock condition.
  • CycleDefinition: target FP, reward multiplier, reset list, next-target function, presentation/dialogue.
  • AchievementDefinition: threshold metric, completion state, passive FP/s reward.
  • ProfileSave: customisation, permanent multipliers, achievements, race/equipment state, timestamps, export schema version.

06
Production sequence

Build the causal loop before the content surface

A practical implementation order for reproducing the observed promise while keeping the prototype testable at every step.

  1. Build the moving road/HUD and map one manual pedal to visible forward motion plus FP.
  2. Add auto-pedalling, training costs, FP/s, cadence/power display, and terrain-driven speed presentation.
  3. Add the first cycle reset and make the next 60 seconds visibly faster; then generate later targets from a clear curve.
  4. Add achievements and passing riders before races so milestones interrupt passive accumulation.
  5. Add races, money, equipment, specialisation, and robust versioned autosave/export only after the core reset cadence is tuned.

Boundaries and unresolved behaviour

Do not encode these as facts yet.
  • Race interaction, race rewards, equipment statistics, opponents, and specialisation were not reached.
  • The exact formulas coupling watts, cadence, incline, speed, distance, and FP production need instrumentation.
  • Offline progress and real reload/import correctness were not tested despite visible persistence controls.
